candidates.section_heading: How to document flood damage > Document everything before you start cleanup
candidates.original_passage: Take clear pictures and videos of damaged items before cleaning, fixing or throwing them out. Capture wide shots and close-ups of walls, floors and furniture. Remember to record serial numbers from electronics and appliances to support your claim.
candidates.proposed_chunk: Take clear pictures and videos of damaged items before cleaning, fixing or throwing them out. Capture wide shots and close-ups of walls, floors and furniture. Remember to record serial numbers from electronics and appliances to support your claim.

surrounding_context.section_heading: How to document flood damage > Document everything before you start cleanup
surrounding_context.guidance_text: Take clear pictures and videos of damaged items before cleaning, fixing or throwing them out. Capture wide shots and close-ups of walls, floors and furniture. Remember to record serial numbers from electronics and appliances to support your claim.

Recovery begins once floodwaters recede. If you have flood insurance, you don’t have to go through it alone.
When it’s safe to return home, act quickly to document flood damage. Early action can support your flood insurance claim and gets you on the road to recovery.

surrounding_context.section_heading: How to document flood damage > FAQs about documenting flood damage and mold
surrounding_context.guidance_text:
Photos and videos are key for your flood insurance claim. Be sure to capture:
Water levels on walls, furniture and appliances.
Structural damage to floors, ceilings and foundations.
Serial numbers on damaged electronics and appliances.
After taking photos, immediately throw away anything that could be a health risk, like spoiled food or moldy clothing, cushions and pillows.

candidates.original_passage:

Small pieces of damaged carpet, drywall or insulation.
Receipts for repairs and replacement items.
Warranty or manufacturer details for replaced appliances.

candidates.proposed_chunk: Learn where to search for temporary housing or a shelter near you.

surrounding_context.section_heading: How to find housing after a disaster
surrounding_context.guidance_text: Learn where to search for temporary housing or a shelter near you. Find out if you qualify for financial help to pay for housing after a disaster.

surrounding_context.section_heading: How to find housing after a disaster > Find a shelter
surrounding_context.guidance_text: If you live in a presidentially declared disaster area, there are programs and organizations that can help you find shelter.

surrounding_context.section_heading: How to find housing after a disaster > Find a shelter > Find transitional shelter in a hotel
surrounding_context.guidance_text:
After you register for disaster assistance with FEMA, you will find out if you qualify for transitional housing. The Transitional Sheltering Assistance (TSA) program will pay for your hotel stay while you are displaced. 
Enter your FEMA registration number to find a hotel that participates in the TSA program and contact them to reserve a room.

candidates.section_heading: How to find housing after a disaster > Get help paying for housing
candidates.original_passage: Some Low Income Home Energy Assistance Programs (LIHEAPs) set aside money to help people get shelter after a natural disaster. Each office sets its own criteria for who can receive funds. Contact the LIHEAP office that serves your state. Or contact the LIHEAP office in your tribal area.
